content.value_statement: Vague prompts often produce incomplete or inconsistent AI responses. This skill gives clear structures, examples, and iteration methods for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains clarity, context, and specificity principles for prompt writing.
Describes zero-shot, few-shot, step-by-step, and role prompting techniques.
Provides reusable prompt structures for general and coding requests.
Shows common prompt anti-patterns with improved alternatives.
Outlines system prompt sections and an iteration process.
limitations: It is a text guide only and does not run tests or inspect projects.
It does not include automation scripts or external integrations.
Examples focus mainly on coding and assistant design workflows.
Some source text is Korean, so some users may need translation.

use_cases.title: Improve Coding Requests
use_cases.description: Create precise prompts that include environment, current state, goal, and constraints for coding assistance.

use_cases.title: Design Assistant Instructions
use_cases.description: Draft system prompts that define identity, capabilities, constraints, response format, and examples.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Prompting
use_cases.description: Give teams a shared structure for task prompts, review prompts, and prompt iteration.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Basic Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this vague request into a clear AI prompt. Include the task, context, expected output, and any missing questions: [request]

prompt_templates.title: Add Context to a Coding Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a coding prompt using these details: environment, current behavior, target behavior, error message, relevant files, and constraints. Details: [details]

prompt_templates.title: Create a Few-Shot Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a few-shot prompt for this task. Include two input and output examples, then add the real input: [task and input]

prompt_templates.title: Design a System Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a system prompt for an AI assistant. Define identity, capabilities, limits, safety boundaries, response format, and example interactions: [assistant goal]

output_examples.input: Improve this request: Fix my login bug.
output_examples.output: Please help debug a login failure in my application. I will provide the framework, authentication flow, error message, expected behavior, and relevant files.

output_examples.input: Create a prompt structure for a code review assistant.
output: Define the assistant role and review scope.
List the project conventions and constraints.
Ask for findings ordered by severity with file references.
Request concise suggestions and note any missing context.

best_practices: State the role, task, context, constraints, and expected format.
Include short examples when output style or evaluation criteria matter.
Iterate on prompts by comparing results against concrete success criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not ask broad open-ended questions without scope or success criteria.
Do not bury the main request under unrelated background.
Do not rely on negative instructions when a direct positive instruction is clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create clearer prompts, prompt structures, and system prompts for AI assistants.

faq.question: Can it write prompts for coding tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes structures for environment, current state, goals, dependencies, and constraints.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown guide and does not include runnable scripts.

faq.question: Is it useful for system prompts?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines identity, capabilities, constraints, response format, and example sections.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with clarity, context, and specificity before advanced templates.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
